name: Snow Quartz
physical: Crystal healers link it to a sense of calm and purity
Many people keep it nearby for restful evenings
summary: Snow Quartz is milky white quartz, gentle and abundant, a stone of purity, stillness and quiet resets in crystal healing tradition and meditation.
intro: Snow quartz, also called milky quartz, is white to creamy quartz that looks clouded like frosted glass. The milky color comes from countless tiny fluid-filled bubbles trapped inside as the crystal grew, which scatter light so it cannot pass through cleanly. It is one of the most common forms of quartz, found in veins, boulders and big crystal points around the world. Snow quartz is usually inexpensive and takes a smooth polish, making it popular for beads, spheres and tumbled stones. Its soft, quiet look pairs well with nearly any other crystal in a collection.
history: Milky quartz has been used by people for thousands of years, both as a tool stone and in ceremony. In some Native American traditions, white quartz is considered sacred, associated with the moon or the spirit world. In Japan, white quartz stones often decorate Shinto shrines, where their color symbolizes purity. In Ireland, white quartz pebbles were placed on ancient burial mounds such as Newgrange. The name snow quartz is a modern trade term for the milky white variety. It was a convenient, easily carved stone for early cultures and remains widely available today.
meaning: Snow quartz is a stone of purity and peace in crystal tradition. Its soft white color is linked to the crown and third eye chakras, and practitioners say it brings stillness, balance and clear energy. It is often used to wipe the slate clean after an emotional period, or to bring a quiet mood to a home. Snow quartz is also considered a gentle stone, ideal for beginners and sensitive people. Emotionally it is associated with patience, reducing frustration and softening reactions. Many use it in meditation to focus on breathing and let thoughts drift away. Some healers pair it with moonlight rituals because of its milky color. Physical associations are restful: a relaxed, settled feeling in the evening.
howToUse: Hold a snow quartz in your palm and watch your breath slow as you meditate in a quiet room. Place a polished piece or sphere on a bedside table to encourage a calm bedtime routine. Set a few stones along a windowsill during a new moon to represent a fresh start. Wear snow quartz beads as a bracelet on days that need patience. Add it to a grid with amethyst and selenite for peace. Carry a small stone in your pocket as a calming anchor during busy days, and place it in a bowl in your entryway to welcome a peaceful atmosphere.
care: Snow quartz is hard and stable, so you can rinse it in cool water, dry it with a soft cloth and cleanse it in moonlight, sunlight, smoke or sound. A bowl of sea salt overnight is safe for solid pieces. Avoid sudden temperature changes if the piece has natural fractures, and skip ultrasonic cleaners for cracked stones. Store it separately from softer stones, since quartz can scratch them, and wrap polished spheres to keep them glossy.
identify: Genuine snow quartz is cool, heavy for its size and shows a cloudy, greasy to glassy luster with natural internal fractures. Cheap imitations include white glass or plastic, which feel warm and may contain bubbles or seams. Dyed or bleached stones are rare but exist. Snow quartz can be confused with calcite, magnesite or howlite, which are much softer and will scratch easily. Quartz will scratch glass, and it does not fizz in vinegar like calcite.

faq.q: What is snow quartz good for?
faq.a: Snow quartz is traditionally used for peace, stillness and fresh starts. Crystal healers link it to the crown and third eye chakras and recommend it for meditation and restful evenings.

faq.q: Is snow quartz the same as milky quartz?
faq.a: Yes. Snow quartz is a trade name for milky quartz, which gets its white color from many tiny fluid-filled bubbles trapped inside the crystal as it formed.

faq.q: Can snow quartz go in water and sun?
faq.a: Yes, snow quartz is hard and stable, so it can be rinsed and placed in sunlight. Avoid sudden temperature shifts if it has fractures, and dry it with a soft cloth after washing.
